title: The Field of Play
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 1, The Field of Play. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Field of Play — Field surface
body: Natural, artificial or permitted hybrid surface; artificial turf must be green and meet applicable quality standards.

title: The Field of Play — Goals
body: Goals must meet the required dimensions, be safely secured and use approved posts and crossbar.

title: The Field of Play — Goal Line Technology (GLT)
body: Approved GLT may assist with goal decisions and must meet IFAB requirements.

title: The Field of Play — Commercial advertising
body: Restricts advertising on the field, goal nets, technical areas and related equipment.

title: The Field of Play — Logos and emblems
body: Restricts team, competition and manufacturer logos on the field and goal equipment.

title: The Field of Play — Video assistant referees (VARs)
body: Sets field-of-play requirements for the video operation room and referee review area where VAR is used.

title: The Field of Play — Field markings
body: Rectangular field, boundary and halfway lines, centre mark and circle; unauthorised marks can be cautioned.

title: The Field of Play — Dimensions
body: Competition sets field dimensions within the Law's permitted length and width ranges.

title: The Field of Play — Dimensions for international matches
body: International matches use the narrower dimensions specified by the Law.

title: The Field of Play — The goal area
body: Defines the goal area from lines measured 5.5 m from each goalpost and parallel to the goal line.

title: The Field of Play — The penalty area
body: Defines the penalty area and places the penalty mark 11 m from the goal line midpoint.

title: The Field of Play — The corner area
body: A quarter-circle arc at each corner flag defines where corner kicks are taken.

title: The Field of Play — Flagposts
body: Corner flagposts are required, at least 1.5 m high and with a non-pointed top.

title: The Field of Play — The technical area
body: Defines the permitted bench and team-official area and its conduct requirements.

title: The Ball
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 2, The Ball. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Ball — Qualities and measurements
body: The ball must be spherical and meet the Law's material, circumference, weight and pressure requirements.

title: The Ball — Replacement of a defective ball
body: Stop play to replace a defective ball; restart with a dropped ball if it became defective during play.

title: The Ball — Additional balls
body: Additional balls may be placed around the field if they meet the same requirements and are controlled by the referee.

title: The Players
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 3, The Players. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Players — Number of players
body: Each team may field up to eleven players, including a goalkeeper; a match normally cannot continue below seven, subject to protocol exceptions and competition forfeiture rules.

title: The Players — Team captain
body: The captain has no special status under the Laws but is responsible for team behaviour and may be addressed by the referee.

title: The Players — Number of substitutions
body: Competition rules set substitutions; senior A international friendlies allow eight, or up to eleven by prior agreement, with three substitution opportunities.

title: The Players — Substitution procedure
body: The outgoing player must leave within ten seconds of the signal; if late, the substitute waits until the first stoppage after one minute of running time following the restart.

title: The Players — Changing the goalkeeper
body: Any player may change places with the goalkeeper.

title: The Players — Offences and sanctions
body: A late outgoing player must still leave; the substitution cannot be cancelled, and a caution applies only for excessive delay beyond the time limit.

title: The Players — Players and substitutes sent off
body: A player sent off before or after kick-off cannot take part; the Law sets how the team may replace or not replace them.

title: The Players — Extra persons on the field of play
body: Sets how referees deal with team officials, substitutes, sent-off players and other extra persons on the field.

title: The Players — Player outside the field of play
body: Covers temporary exits, re-entry permission and a goalkeeper leaving the field during play.

title: The Players — Goal scored with an extra person on the field of play
body: The referee applies the Law's goal-validity and restart tests when an extra person is on the field.

title: The Players' Equipment
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 4, The Players' Equipment. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Players' Equipment — Safety
body: Equipment must not be dangerous; non-dangerous accessories are permitted only when safely and securely covered.

title: The Players' Equipment — Compulsory equipment
body: Shirt with sleeves, shorts, socks, shinguards and footwear are required.

title: The Players' Equipment — Colours
body: Each team's colours must distinguish players from opponents and match officials; goalkeeper colours have additional requirements.

title: The Players' Equipment — Other equipment
body: Protective and performance equipment is allowed if safe; accessories must be non-dangerous and securely covered.

title: The Players' Equipment — Slogans, statements, images and advertising
body: Sets limits on messages, images and advertising on player equipment.

title: The Players' Equipment — Offences and sanctions
body: Officials inspect equipment; players must correct dangerous or unauthorised items before entering or continuing.

title: The Referee
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 5, The Referee. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Referee — The authority of the referee
body: The referee has full authority to enforce the Laws from arrival for the pre-match inspection until leaving the field after the match.

title: The Referee — Decisions of the referee
body: The referee decides facts connected with play; competitions may authorise technology for VAR, goal-line and offside decisions.

title: The Referee — Powers and duties
body: Includes discipline, advantage, managing injuries and stoppages; advantage may apply after an incorrect restart if opponents benefit.

title: The Referee — Video assistant referee (VAR)
body: VAR may review the Law's reviewable incidents, including a clearly incorrect second caution leading to a red card; optional corner review is not adopted by the Premier League for 2026/27.

title: The Referee — Referee's equipment
body: Referees may use approved communication and technology; competitions may provide controlled body cameras, and safe covered accessories are allowed.

title: The Referee — Referee signals
body: Prescribes the referee's signals for restarts, disciplinary action, advantage and VAR-related decisions.

title: The Referee — Liability of match officials
body: Match officials are not liable for specified injury, property or other loss arising from decisions made under the Laws.

title: The Other Match Officials
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 6, The Other Match Officials. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Other Match Officials — Assistant referees
body: Assist with ball-out, offside, substitutions and other incidents within their view.

title: The Other Match Officials — Fourth official
body: Supports substitutions, technical-area management, added time and other referee duties.

title: The Other Match Officials — Additional assistant referees
body: Provide additional goal-line and penalty-area assistance where appointed.

title: The Other Match Officials — Reserve assistant referee
body: May replace an assistant referee who cannot continue.

title: The Other Match Officials — Video match officials
body: VAR and AVAR roles follow the VAR protocol, including the 2026/27 reviewable-incident changes.

title: The Other Match Officials — Assistant referee signals
body: Prescribes flag signals for throw-ins, goal kicks, corners, offside and substitutions.

title: The Other Match Officials — Additional assistant referee signals
body: Prescribes signals used by additional assistant referees.

title: The Duration of the Match
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 7, The Duration of the Match. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Duration of the Match — Periods of play
body: Two equal halves; duration set by competition.

title: The Duration of the Match — Half-time interval
body: Must not exceed 15 minutes unless competition rules.

title: The Duration of the Match — Allowance for time lost
body: Added time for substitutions, injuries, VAR, etc.

title: The Duration of the Match — Penalty kick
body: A penalty kick is completed even if time expires before it is taken.

title: The Duration of the Match — Abandoned match
body: An abandoned match is replayed unless competition rules or organisers decide otherwise; a team responsible for dropping below seven may forfeit.

title: The Start and Restart of Play
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 8, The Start and Restart of Play. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Start and Restart of Play — Kick-off
body: Start of each half and after goals; ball in play when kicked.

title: The Start and Restart of Play — Dropped ball
body: Drop for the team that would retain or gain possession, including the team entitled to the next restart; after contact with an official or outside agent, drop where the contact occurred.

title: The Ball In and Out of Play
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 9, The Ball In and Out of Play. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Ball In and Out of Play — Ball out of play
body: The whole ball must cross a goal line or touchline, or play must be stopped by the referee.

title: The Ball In and Out of Play — Ball in play
body: The ball remains in play at all other times, including rebounds from goalposts, crossbar and match officials unless the Law says otherwise.

title: Determining the Outcome of a Match
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 10, Determining the Outcome of a Match. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: Determining the Outcome of a Match — Goal scored
body: Whole ball over the goal line between posts and under crossbar.

title: Determining the Outcome of a Match — Winning team
body: Team scoring more goals wins.

title: Determining the Outcome of a Match — Penalties (penalty shoot-out)
body: Sets the procedure for kicks from the penalty mark, including the 2026/27 accidental double-touch clarification.

title: Offside
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 11, Offside. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: Offside — Offside position
body: Nearer opponents' goal line than ball and second-last opponent.

title: Offside — Offside offence
body: Involvement in active play from an offside position.

title: Offside — No offence
body: Level with second-last opponent; in own half; from goal kick, throw-in, corner.

title: Offside — Offences and sanctions
body: An offside offence gives an indirect free kick; interference and deliberate play are assessed under the Law.

title: Fouls and Misconduct
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 12, Fouls and Misconduct. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: Fouls and Misconduct — Direct free kick
body: Careless, reckless or excessive force; handball; holding; etc.

title: Fouls and Misconduct — Indirect free kick
body: Dangerous play, impeding, dissent, goalkeeper offences.

title: Fouls and Misconduct — Corner kick
body: A corner may be awarded when the goalkeeper holds the ball for more than eight seconds or a team delays its goal kick.

title: Fouls and Misconduct — Disciplinary action
body: Covers cautions, send-offs and DOGSO; DOGSO assessment includes attackers, and no sanction follows if advantage leads to a goal. Optional send-offs for covered-mouth abuse or protest walk-offs are not adopted by the Premier League for 2026/27.

title: Fouls and Misconduct — Restart of play after fouls and misconduct
body: Sets the restart after an offence, including direct or indirect free kicks, penalties, corners and dropped balls.

title: Denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity
body: Consider distance to goal, direction, likelihood of control and the location and number of defenders and attackers; if advantage results in a goal, there is no sanction.

title: Handling the ball
body: Deliberate hand/arm contact, unnaturally enlarged body, or scoring/handling offences; upper arm boundary at armpit.

title: Serious foul play
body: A tackle or challenge that endangers an opponent's safety or uses excessive force/brutality is serious foul play and requires a sending-off.

title: Violent conduct
body: Using or attempting excessive force or brutality when not challenging for the ball.

title: Direct free kick — careless, reckless or excessive force
body: A direct free kick is awarded if a player commits a physical offence against an opponent in a careless or reckless manner, or uses excessive force or brutality.

title: Indirect free kick
body: An indirect free kick is awarded for offences such as dangerous play, impeding without contact and specified goalkeeper offences.

title: Corner kick as a sanction
body: A corner may be awarded when the goalkeeper controls the ball with the hands/arms for more than eight seconds or a team delays its goal kick.

title: Disciplinary action
body: Cautions and send-offs cover unsporting behaviour, serious foul play, violent conduct and DOGSO; DOGSO assessment includes attackers, and advantage leading to a goal carries no sanction.

title: Free Kicks
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 13, Free Kicks. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: Free Kicks — Types of free kick
body: Direct and indirect free kicks.

title: Free Kicks — Procedure
body: The ball is stationary, opponents keep the required distance, and the ball is in play when kicked and clearly moves.

title: Free Kicks — Offences and sanctions
body: Covers encroachment, second touches and other infringements of free-kick procedure.

title: The Penalty Kick
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 14, The Penalty Kick. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Penalty Kick — Introduction
body: A penalty kick is awarded for a direct-free-kick offence by a player inside their own penalty area.

title: The Penalty Kick — Procedure
body: The ball is placed on the mark; the goalkeeper and other players must meet the Law's position and timing requirements.

title: The Penalty Kick — Offences and sanctions
body: Covers encroachment, feinting, goalkeeper offences and accidental double touches; an accidental double touch results in a retake if scored or an indirect free kick if missed.

title: The Penalty Kick — Summary table
body: Summarises the restart and outcome for penalty-kick infringements by the kicker, goalkeeper and other players.

title: The Throw-in
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 15, The Throw-in. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Throw-in — Introduction
body: A throw-in restarts play when the whole ball crosses the touchline; a five-second countdown can transfer a delayed throw-in to opponents.

title: The Throw-in — Procedure
body: The thrower faces the field, uses both hands and delivers the ball from behind and over the head while observing foot placement.

title: The Throw-in — Offences and sanctions
body: For deliberate delay, the referee starts a visual five-second countdown; if no throw is taken, the opponents receive it.

title: The Goal Kick
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 16, The Goal Kick. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Goal Kick — Introduction
body: A goal kick restarts play after an attacking touch sends the whole ball over the goal line without a goal.

title: The Goal Kick — Procedure
body: The kick is taken from the goal area; opponents remain outside the penalty area until the ball is in play.

title: The Goal Kick — Offences and sanctions
body: A visual five-second countdown applies to deliberate delay; if the kick is not taken, opponents receive a corner.

title: The Corner Kick
body: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 — Law 17, The Corner Kick. Applies in Premier League matches alongside 2026/27 competition guidance.

title: The Corner Kick — Introduction
body: A corner follows a defender's last touch over the goal line; it may also follow a goalkeeper holding the ball over eight seconds or a delayed goal kick.

title: The Corner Kick — Procedure
body: The ball is placed in the corner area; opponents stay at least 9.15 m away until it is in play.

title: The Corner Kick — Offences and sanctions
body: Covers encroachment, a second touch and other infringements of corner-kick procedure.

title: Incorrectly awarded corner kick
body: IFAB permits competitions to review a clearly incorrect corner only when the decision can be corrected immediately without delaying the restart; the Premier League does not adopt this option for 2026/27.

title: Mistaken identity
body: VAR may correct a caution or sending-off shown to the wrong player when another player of either team committed the offence.

title: Goal/no goal — offside
body: Offside in the build-up or at goal may be reviewed; factual line decisions use VAR-only review where appropriate.

title: Penalty / no penalty
body: Location of offence, handball or foul in the box, and incorrect award or missed penalty.

title: VAR protocol 2026/27
body: VAR may assist only for clear and obvious errors or serious missed incidents in reviewable categories; the referee makes the final decision.

title: Clearly incorrect second caution
body: A red card resulting from a clearly incorrect second caution is reviewable; a potential second caution is not a separate review category.

title: Principles
body: VAR remains a match-official support tool; the referee makes an initial decision and retains final authority.

title: Reviewable decisions
body: Goal/no goal, penalty/no penalty, red cards including a clearly incorrect second caution, and mistaken identity; incorrect corners are an optional review category.

title: Review threshold
body: Intervention requires a clear and obvious error or serious missed incident; the optional corner review must be corrected immediately without delaying the restart.

title: Procedures
body: Check, review, on-field review (OFR), VAR-only review, communication to players.

title: Premier League — Laws of the Game
body: Premier League matches follow the IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 and the Premier League Handbook 2026/27, including the League's competition choices and refereeing guidance.

title: High threshold for penalising challenges
body: Not every contact is a foul; maintain the high threshold while protecting player safety.

title: Premier League Football Principles — 2026/27
body: Maintain a high threshold for on-field challenges and VAR while protecting player safety; improve SAOT/VAR efficiency, participant behaviour and measures against time-wasting.

title: Five-second goal-kick countdown
body: For a clearly delayed goal kick, the referee starts a visible five-second countdown; if it expires, the opponents receive a corner kick.

title: Challenges affecting goalkeepers
body: Penalise a clear attacking action with no intent to play or challenge for the ball when contact unfairly affects the goalkeeper's ability to play or challenge for it.

title: Hair-pulling sanctions
body: A clear, deliberate hair pull with excessive force or brutality is a red card; without excessive force or brutality it is a yellow card.

title: Proportionate handball decisions
body: Continue the Premier League's 'less is more' approach to penalising handball.

title: Material holding actions
body: Penalise clear, sustained or impactful holding, especially when a defender focuses on the opponent rather than playing or challenging for the ball.

title: One-minute return delay after treatment
body: Players treated or assessed on the field, or whose injury stops play, must leave for at least one minute after play restarts, subject to the Law's exceptions.

title: Refereeing Points of Emphasis — 2026/27
body: The Premier League's seasonal guidance focuses on holding, challenges affecting goalkeepers, hair-pulling sanctions, handball, and simulation/embellishment.

title: Match-flow requirements — 2026/27
body: The Premier League implements one-minute post-treatment exits, a ten-second substitution exit limit and five-second throw-in/goal-kick countdowns.

title: Simulation and embellishment
body: Continue to address clear actions intended to deceive the referee, including simulation and embellishment.

title: Ten-second substitution exit limit
body: The outgoing player must leave within ten seconds; if not, the substitute waits until the first stoppage after one minute of running time following the restart.

title: Technical area conduct
body: Behaviour of coaches and staff; sanctions aligned with Law 12 team official offences.

title: Five-second throw-in countdown
body: For a clearly delayed throw-in, the referee starts a visible five-second countdown; if it expires, the throw-in is awarded to the opponents.

title: High threshold for VAR intervention
body: The referee's call stands unless evidence readily available to VAR shows a clear and obvious error; improve efficiency and reduce delays.

title: Premier League — VAR in 2026/27
body: Applies IFAB VAR rules with the Premier League's high intervention threshold; the League adopts second-yellow-to-red reviews but not the optional review of incorrectly awarded corners.

title: Offside and semi-automated offside
body: Use semi-automated offside technology to improve efficiency and reduce delays while retaining the clear-and-obvious VAR threshold.

title: Second yellow resulting in a red card
body: A VAR review applies when a clearly incorrect second yellow results in a red card; a potential second yellow is not reviewed as a separate incident.
